question: What is the main effect of a sedative drug?

options.B: Increases heart rate and blood pressure
options.C: Calms anxiety and reduces motor activity

explanation: Sedatives are given to reduce anxiety and calm a patient without forcing them to sleep. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h1)

question: What factor determines whether a medication acts as a sedative or a hypnotic?

options.A: The specific time of day it is swallowed
options.B: The weight and age of the pregnant woman
options.C: The administered dose of the drug
options.D: The method used to manufacture the pill

explanation: Lower doses produce a calming sedative effect, while higher doses of the same medication induce sleep as a hypnotic. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain do benzodiazepines enhance to create a calming effect?
explanation: Benzodiazepines attach to receptors that boost the natural calming actions of GABA in the central nervous system. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do benzodiazepines affect nerve cells to lower central nervous system activity?

options.A: They speed up electrical impulses between brain synapses
options.B: They block all blood flow to the cerebral cortex
options.C: They destroy excess neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft
options.D: They allow chloride ions to enter and hyperpolarize the neuron

explanation: Chloride ions enter the nerve cell, making the inside more negative and harder for the neuron to fire. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why are barbiturates much more dangerous than modern sedatives during an overdose?

options.A: They permanently damage the heart muscle on contact
options.B: They cannot be reversed by any known medical antidote
options.C: They cause immediate kidney failure within minutes
options.D: They lack a ceiling effect for respiratory depression

explanation: Barbiturates continue to suppress breathing as the dose increases, which can easily lead to fatal respiratory arrest. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why are barbiturates rarely used for pregnant women today?

options.A: They are completely illegal to manufacture globally
options.B: Safer options exist with lower risks of fatal overdose and dependence
options.C: They cause permanent blindness in developing fetuses
options.D: They have zero effect on central nervous system activity

explanation: High toxicity and strong potential for abuse mean clinical practice now favors benzodiazepines and non-benzodiazepines. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is floppy infant syndrome in a newborn exposed to long-term sedatives?

options.A: High fever, tremors, and excessive crying
options.C: Premature fusion of the cranial skull bones
options.D: Rapid heart rate and constant muscle twitching

explanation: Babies exposed to high levels of sedatives late in pregnancy often struggle with muscle tone, body temperature, and breathing at birth. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h4)

question: A breastfeeding mother takes a prescribed hypnotic medication nightly. What sign in her infant needs immediate reporting?

options.B: Excessive sleepiness and poor feeding habits
options.C: Bright yellow discoloration of the skin
options.D: Sudden weight gain over a twenty-four hour period

explanation: Sedatives pass into breast milk, so an unusually drowsy baby who refuses to feed points to potential drug toxicity. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h4)

question: What term describes needing higher drug doses over time to get the same initial effect?
explanation: Tolerance happens when the body adapts to a medication, requiring an increase in dosage to achieve the same clinical result. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why must midwives support gradual dose reduction instead of sudden stoppage for a dependent pregnant patient?

options.A: Sudden cessation immediately causes complete liver failure
options.B: Gradual tapering prevents the baby from growing too fast
options.C: Abrupt stopping triggers dangerous withdrawal symptoms like seizures
options.D: Quick withdrawal stops the placenta from functioning properly

explanation: Stopping central nervous system depressants suddenly sends the nervous system into overdrive, risking severe seizures and fetal distress. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which vital sign needs the closest monitoring after a patient receives a sedative medication?
explanation: Sedatives depress the central nervous system, making it essential to monitor breathing rate to catch dangerous slowing early. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary role of a reversal agent like flumazenil in an emergency?

options.A: It blocks the drug from receptor sites to reverse sedation
options.B: It lowers the maternal blood pressure to safe levels
options.C: It permanently cures the underlying anxiety disorder
options.D: It speeds up the digestive system to expel the pill

explanation: Reversal agents compete for and block the same receptor sites, quickly counteracting sedative effects in an overdose. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h6)
